extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2026 reviewers (program committee members, area chairs, senior area chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Official instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewers of ICML 2026 submissions, covering reviewer responsibilities, ethical rules, review-form questions and rating scales, position-paper-specific criteria, LLM-use policy, and procedural guidance for bidding, discussion, and final justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: List of duties reviewers must perform for ICML review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate areas of expertise and bid on submissions; check assignments and notify the area chair of problems (e.g., conflicts of interest); carefully review correctness and merits of assigned submissions; follow your assigned actual policy for LLM use in reviewing (displayed on Reviewer Console); read and acknowledge the Authors’ Responses; actively participate in discussions (three rounds: rebuttal, reviewer follow-up, author follow-up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting Area Chair First
rubrics_metrics.description: Who to contact when encountering problems or questions about an assigned paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assigned area chair (AC) for a paper should be your first point of contact; contact the AC by leaving a comment in OpenReview with the AC as a reader. If unresolved, contact program chairs via provided channels but refrain from emailing PCs directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and Non-use of Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All information related to submitted manuscripts, reviews, and discussions is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until public; do not talk about or share submissions without prior approval from program chairs. Code submitted for review cannot be distributed or used for any other purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Collusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any form of collusion between authors and reviewers/ACs/SACs is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit or tacit arrangements to obtain favorable reviews are prohibited. Report suspected collusion via the Ethics Violation Reporting form. Violations may lead to sanctions or rejection (see Peer Review Ethics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Suspected Ethical Violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for reporting suspected unethical conduct in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe someone is engaging in unethical conduct, notify ICML via the Ethics Violation Reporting form. Suspected violations will be investigated by program chairs, the integrity chair, or the ICML Oversight Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI / LLM Use Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must follow the LLM/Generative AI policy assigned to them for reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow their assigned actual policy for LLM use in reviewing, as displayed on the Reviewer Console. Any deviation from the assigned policy constitutes a violation of peer-review ethics and may result in penalties (e.g., desk rejection of the reviewer’s submissions). Position track reviewers must adhere to the conservative (no LLM) policy. Authors may use generative AI but remain responsible for all content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt Injection Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt injection by authors is forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICML integrity chairs and program chairs will use prompt-injection detectors. If you suspect prompt injection, report it via the Ethics Violation Reporting form and continue to review the paper normally. Update (2/14/2026): prompts that merely seek to detect LLM use by reviewers will not be penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding Principle for Reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Review the papers of others as you would wish your own to be reviewed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing should create value for authors (actionable feedback) and for the community (helping select and improve papers). Maintain professional conduct: be polite, respectful, and avoid unprofessional reviews that may harm authors or the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Thoughtful
rubrics_metrics.description: A best-practice expectation: take care when reviewing, mindful of authors' circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that submissions may come from first-year students or first-time submitters; avoid crushing spirits and provide constructive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Fair
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid personal bias influencing your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let personal feelings affect assessments; avoid discriminatory criteria unrelated to scientific content or clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should provide actionable value to authors, other reviewers, and ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive feedback and suggestions for improvement rather than terse judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague statements in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete examples and substantiation for claims about strengths or weaknesses so authors can address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Flexible
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow authors to address points during discussion and update your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may address issues in rebuttal; reviewers should update their understanding and revise reviews when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines and respond promptly during discussion periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot complete a review on time, notify the AC promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips for Reviewing — Read Carefully and Take Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice on how to approach reading an assigned paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-read the Review Form first, read the paper carefully and critically with empathy, take notes (highlight main contributions, mark sections to recheck), and bear in mind you must provide an evaluation on the Review Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Claims and Substantiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper properly substantiates its claimed contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may involve checking proofs, ensuring hypotheses are tested by experiments, and verifying empirical claims follow from results. Focus effort on major issues that threaten central contributions; note minor, easily fixed problems but prioritize critical flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization with Prior Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper positions itself relative to existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if missing citations would change conclusions. It's often unnecessary to cite all related work; judge whether omitted works would affect the paper's claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate Strengths and Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claims about strengths and weaknesses must be supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence or reasoning for each identified strength/weakness so authors and ACs can understand and act on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (Review Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise, neutral summary of the paper and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly summarize the paper in your own words (not the abstract) without critique; a well-written summary should not be disputed by the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses (Review Form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough assessment touching on soundness, presentation, significance, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss each dimension and substantiate claims. Be open-minded about broad definitions of significance and originality; provide constructive suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness (Review Dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the submission is technically sound and claims are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess correctness, rigor, and methodological appropriateness; for theory, check proofs and assumptions; for experiments, check design and honesty in evaluation. Soundness is distinct from impact. Rating scale: 4 (excellent), 3 (good), 2 (fair), 1 (poor). If you select fair or poor, ensure the Strengths and Weaknesses justify the rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (Review Dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of writing, structure, and contextualization relative to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge clarity and organization; does the paper provide enough information for an expert to reproduce results? Rating scale: 4 (excellent), 3 (good), 2 (fair), 1 (poor). If fair/poor, include justification in Strengths and Weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (Review Dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance and potential impact of the paper's contribution to machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the paper addresses an important problem, advances understanding or practice, and could influence future research or applications. Scope of impact may be broad or specialized. Rating scale: 4 (excellent), 3 (good), 2 (fair), 1 (poor). If fair/poor, justify in Strengths and Weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (Review Dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the work provides new insights or contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty of ideas, methods, tasks, theory, data, or perspectives; novel combinations of existing techniques can be original. Distinguish contributions from closely related literature and justify claimed novelty. Rating scale: 4 (excellent), 3 (good), 2 (fair), 1 (poor). If fair/poor, justify in Strengths and Weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Questions for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: When to ask authors questions and how to format them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have important questions (ideally 3–5) that could change your evaluation or clarify critical points, number them so authors can respond easily and explain how answers would affect your score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and Societal Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether authors adequately discuss limitations and potential negative societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adequately discussed, enter 'yes'; otherwise give constructive suggestions. Authors should be rewarded, not punished, for upfront discussion of limitations and negative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation (6-point scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall paper recommendation on a 1–6 scale with defined meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choices and guidance: 6 Strong Accept (technically flawless, exceptional impact); 5 Accept (technically solid, high or moderate-high impact); 4 Weak accept (solid advance but some weaknesses; use sparingly); 3 Weak reject (merits but weaknesses outweigh); 2 Reject (technical flaws, weak evaluation, poor reproducibility, unaddressed ethics, or incomprehensible writing); 1 Strong Reject (well-known results, unaddressed ethics, or incomprehensible). Explain and justify choice in Strengths and Weaknesses and final justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer’s self-assessed confidence in their evaluation (1–5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain (familiar, checked details); 4 = confident but not certain; 3 = fairly confident (possible misunderstandings, math/details not carefully checked); 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with central parts; 1 = educated guess (not in your area). Use this to indicate reliability of your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns Flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagging a paper for ethics review and selecting relevant expertise areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe there are ethical issues, flag the paper for ethics review and select areas (e.g., bias, potential harmful applications, privacy, legal compliance, research integrity). Provide detailed explanation of concerns to help ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Affirmations (LLM policy & Code of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer must affirm compliance with assigned LLM policy and ICML code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit checkboxes on the review form require affirming full compliance with the ICML 2026 LLM policy assigned to you and the ICML code of conduct; deviations are violations and may have consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Justification (Post-Rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain final recommendation after considering rebuttal and discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize how you weighed strengths and weaknesses across soundness, originality, significance, and clarity; indicate whether rebuttal addressed main concerns, changed your evaluation, or reinforced it. This text is shared with authors and AC/SAC/PCs and must be constructive, respectful, and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding (Reviewer Assignment Process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers indicate interest/qualifications for submissions during bidding period to aid assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bid on abstracts in OpenReview during the bidding period; these bids will be used in part to assign submissions to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing Process — Read and Update Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for reading assigned submissions, supplemental materials, and updating reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read assigned submissions carefully and critically; reviewers are encouraged (but not required) to read supplementary material. All reviews must be submitted by the deadline. After authors’ responses, reviewers should read and acknowledge them and may engage in one round of additional discussion; update reviews as appropriate before final justification deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC-Reviewer Discussions (Private)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouraged discussion among reviewers and ACs visible only to reviewers and ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to post and respond to notes on OpenReview to resolve contradictions or unclear aspects. These discussions are not visible to authors; reviewers should update reviews to reflect outcomes for authors' benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of Reviews and Opt-in for Rejected Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on public release of reviews and discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and reviewer-author discussions for all accepted papers will be made public on OpenReview after reviewing. Authors of rejected papers may opt-in to public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Concurrent Works
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat recent works that became public shortly before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not required to discuss works made public less than two months before the submission deadline; consider such works concurrent. Use best practices of the subfield; consult the area chair if unsure about citing or evaluating concurrent/unreviewed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper — Clear Statement of Position
rubrics_metrics.description: Position-track papers must clearly state a position on a machine-learning topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper should advocate a position (e.g., policy recommendation, call to action, value statement). If the paper describes technical research without advocating a real position, it is not responsive to the call and should be submitted to the main track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position In Title (Position Paper Requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of a position paper must state the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can a reader understand the paper’s position from the title alone? Examples provided show titles that do or do not state a position; select No if title only lists a topic without a stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Views Section (Mandatory for Position Papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Position papers must include an Alternative Views section in the main body addressing credible opposing positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section is mandatory and must be in the main body (not an appendix); it should describe and address one or more credible opposing positions (not strawmen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper — Paper Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the position paper and the position it advocates (neutral summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief neutral summary of the paper and its advocated position; should not be used to critique and should not be disputed by authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper — Strengths and Weaknesses (Focus on Position)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess strengths and weaknesses of the paper focusing on how well it supports the stated position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the position well supported by reasoning/evidence? Is the topic relevant and likely to inspire discussion? Is the argument clearly presented and appropriately cited? Do not comment on whether you agree with the position; if the paper lacks a position, note that and provide suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper Rating — Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate how well the paper supports its position with reasoning/evidence (4-point scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor. Use this to evaluate clarity and strength of support for the stated position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper Rating — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate how important the position is in terms of scope, impact, timeliness, risks, and benefits (4-point scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor. Consider potential to influence ICML community discussions or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper Rating — Discussion Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the paper's potential to inspire constructive, useful discussion within the ICML community (4-point scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer need not agree with the position. 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper Rating — Argument Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the clarity of presentation and writing style for the position paper (4-point scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper Rating — Related Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate degree to which the paper discusses and cites literature and events relevant to the position (4-point scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position Paper — Questions and Ethics Flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Number important questions for authors and flag ethical issues specific to position papers if present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate numbered questions that could change your opinion. For ethics concerns, flag and select appropriate expertise areas; explain concerns in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Enforcement — LLM Preferences and Assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: New 2026 procedure for reviewers to declare LLM preference and then be assigned a policy per reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During registration, main-track reviewers declare preference between conservative (no LLM) and permissive (LLMs allowed). Once assigned to papers, each reviewer is told which policy to follow for their assigned papers; deviation is a violation and may lead to desk rejection. Note: Position paper track always conservative.
